content: In the field of medicine, inspection refers to the meticulous and deliberate visual examination of a patient, derived from the Latin term Inspectio, meaning the act of observing. This process is conducted using the unaided eye to gather critical clinical information. During the inspection, the examiner carefully observes the following external signs: The physical features of the body, including symmetry and overall appearance. The patient’s nutritional status or body weight. The color of the skin, which may indicate underlying conditions. The frequency and depth of breaths during respiration. The movement of the abdomen and the bilateral chest during the respiratory cycle. The distribution of hair across the body. Any deviation or abnormality in the rectus muscles. The umbilicus, specifically its location, shape, color, and any signs of infiltration or abnormality. The patient’s gait and the manner in which they speak. Additionally, the examiner evaluates for gross deviations, which include: Abnormalities in body contour. The presence of scars or striae (stretch marks). Visible masses or protrusions. Discoloration of the skin or other tissues. Swelling in any region of the body. Tremors or involuntary movements. It is important to note that in clinical practice, inspection is not confined solely to visual information. It often incorporates other sensory observations to enhance diagnostic accuracy.
